metadata.subject: Data Structures
metadata.title: Discover Min Heaps
metadata.description: Insert values into a complete tree and watch the smallest value rise to the root.

learning_objectives: Describe a complete binary tree as the shape of a heap.
Explain why the minimum value stays at the root.

mission.title: Bubble up the minimum
mission.description: Insert values and notice how a smaller child swaps upward toward the root.

introduction.title: A min heap keeps its smallest value on top
introduction.content: A min heap is a complete binary tree stored in an array. Every parent is no larger than its children, so the smallest value is always at the root.
points: New values begin at the next open position.
A value swaps with its parent only when it is smaller.
The tree shape stays complete while values bubble up.

worked_example.title: Insert 10 and bubble it up
worked_example.content: The new value starts at the end, then compares with its parent.

steps.explanation: 10 is placed at the next open position in the complete tree.
10 is smaller than its parent 20, so it swaps upward.
10 is still smaller than 40, so it reaches the root.

worked_example.conclusion: Bubble-up stops when the new value is no smaller than its parent or it reaches the root.

next.title: Now build a min heap.
next.content: Insert one value at a time and watch the root stay smallest.

next-step: The value entered the next open position of the complete tree.
A smaller child swapped with its parent to restore the min-heap rule.
The root remains the smallest value after bubble-up.
Every value is now arranged as a valid min heap.

challenge.start_message: Build the heap by inserting each value and letting smaller values bubble upward.
challenge.continue_message: Challenge complete. Keep inserting values to practise the heap rule.

phases.title: Build the min heap
phases.instruction: Insert all values until YOUR HEAP matches the target array.
phases.feedback: Insert the next value, then swap upward only while it is smaller than its parent.

recall.title: Recall
recall.prompt: In your own words, why does the smallest value stay at the root of a min heap?
recall.model_answer: Each parent is no larger than its children. When a smaller value is inserted, bubble-up swaps carry it toward the root until the min-heap rule is restored.

quiz.question: Where is the minimum value in a min heap?

discovery.title: Min Heap discovery
discovery.summary: A min heap combines a complete tree shape with a parent rule that keeps the smallest value at the root.

sections.title: What?
sections.content: A min heap is a complete binary tree where every parent is no larger than its children.

sections.title: Example
sections.content: Insert 10 below 20, then swap upward until 10 reaches the root.

sections.title: Why?
sections.content: The parent rule makes the smallest value immediately available at the root.

sections.title: Remember
sections.content: Insert at the next open spot → bubble up while the child is smaller.

alternate_explanations.title: Think of a priority line
alternate_explanations.content: The most urgent (smallest) number keeps moving toward the front, while the tree stays complete.

alternate_explanations.title: Walk through one insert
alternate_explanations.content: Add 7 to [30, 18, 24]. Compare 7 with 18, swap, then compare 7 with 30 and swap again.

recall.title: Recall
recall.prompt: In your own words, what happens when a newly inserted heap value is smaller than its parent?
recall.model_answer: The new value swaps upward with its parent until it is no longer smaller or reaches the root.
